name: Transform
requirement_trace: Transform ABC — deterministic pure text transform; approved requirement Chapter 1 Core Contracts; acceptance: 40 transforms importable, each round-trips a sample string

class_attributes.name: name
class_attributes.description: Unique transform identifier; declared as class attribute in each concrete subclass; must be non-empty string

abstract_methods.name: apply
abstract_methods.description: Transform input text and return transformed string. Must be overridden by every concrete subclass. No default implementation.

behavior.description: Deterministic pure text-to-text transformation. Same input always produces same output.
behavior.thread_safety: stateless; safe if subclass has no mutable state

preconditions: text argument must be an instance of str
text may be empty string (len 0 is valid)
caller must not pass None, bytes, or non-str types
postconditions: no files, sockets, or environment variables are modified by apply()
no exception is swallowed silently — domain errors propagate as StressForgeError subclass

idempotency.note: The ABC does not enforce idempotency. Subclasses define their own. E.g., Upper is idempotent; Reverse is involutory (apply(apply(x))==x) but not idempotent.

invariants: name class attribute is always a non-empty str on every concrete subclass
apply() never mutates REGISTRY or any module-level state
apply() never performs I/O (file, network, stdout, stderr)
apply() always returns str given valid str input
instantiating Transform directly raises TypeError (abstract class)

error_taxonomy.TypeError: Raised if text is not str or if Transform is instantiated directly (caller contract violation)
error_taxonomy.StressForgeError: Domain base; subclasses raised by apply() on invalid domain input where explicitly specified by subclass
